t: Oxalosuccinic acid, an intermediate compound of Krebs cycle is a
s: Oxalosuccinic acid is formed by oxidation of isocitric acid (6C) in the Krebs cycle and retains all six carbons. Its decarboxylation then releases CO₂ to form α-ketoglutaric acid (5C). Hence oxalosuccinic acid is a 6-carbon compound.

t: Hydrogen from malate is accepted by
s: Malate is oxidised to oxaloacetate by malate dehydrogenase in the Krebs cycle, and the hydrogen removed is accepted by NAD⁺, forming NADH + H⁺. FAD is the acceptor only at succinate to fumarate, FMN is part of complex I, and ubiquinone is in the ETS.

t: In respiration, the first release of CO₂ is from
s: In aerobic respiration the first CO₂ is released during the link reaction, when pyruvic acid (3C) undergoes oxidative decarboxylation by pyruvate dehydrogenase to form acetyl CoA (2C). CO₂ is later released from oxalosuccinic acid and α-ketoglutaric acid in the Krebs cycle.

t: Phosphorylation of glucose and fructose during glycolysis is catalized by
s: In glycolysis, glucose is phosphorylated to glucose-6-phosphate by hexokinase using ATP, and fructose can likewise be phosphorylated by hexokinase. Invertase hydrolyses sucrose, citrate synthase acts in the Krebs cycle, and pyruvic dehydrogenase converts pyruvate to acetyl CoA.

t: With regarding to Mitochondrial ETS, which of the following possesses 2 copper centres
s: Complex IV, cytochrome c oxidase, contains cytochromes a and a₃ and two copper centres, and transfers electrons to oxygen. Cytochrome c is a small mobile protein without copper centres, and complex III (cytochrome bc₁) contains cytochromes b and c₁ but no copper centres.

t: Ubiquinone receives reducing equivalents via:-
s: Ubiquinone receives reducing equivalents from NADH via complex I (NADH dehydrogenase) and from FADH₂ via complex II (succinate dehydrogenase). Since FADH₂, complex I and complex II all pass electrons to ubiquinone, all the given options are correct.

t: Enzymes involved in glycolysis is present in
s: Glycolysis (EMP pathway) occurs in the cytoplasm of all living organisms, so all its enzymes are present in the cytosol. The Krebs cycle enzymes are in the mitochondrial matrix, and the ETS is located on the inner mitochondrial membrane.

t:
Findout the mis-matched pair:-
[[img:eff3b972ca95]]
s: Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase) does not pump protons, so it is not a proton pump; this pair is mismatched. Complex I contains FMN, complex IV contains two copper centres, and complex III contains cytochromes b and c₁, so these are correct.

t:
Which of the following statements are true :
A) Acetyl Co. A is the common intermediate formed during the aerobic oxidation of carbohydrate, fat and proteins.
B) Glycolysis is the common respiratory pathway of both aerobic and anaerobic respiration
C) Pyruvic acid is formed during respiration only when carbohydrates are used as substrate
D) In glycolysis, there is no consumption of molecular oxygen
E) Four oxidative decarboxylation occur during aerobic respiration when one molecule of glucose is used as substrate.
s: A is true: acetyl CoA is the common intermediate of carbohydrate, fat and protein oxidation. B is true: glycolysis is common to aerobic and anaerobic respiration. D is true: glycolysis uses no O₂. E is true as per the key: 2 oxidative decarboxylations per pyruvate × 2. C is false: pyruvate is formed from other substrates too.

t: Under aerobic condition, what will happen to the pyruvic acid produced during glycolyis?
s: Under aerobic conditions pyruvic acid formed in the cytoplasm enters the mitochondrial matrix, where pyruvate dehydrogenase carries out oxidative decarboxylation to form acetyl CoA, NADH and CO₂. Reduction to ethanol and CO₂ happens in anaerobic conditions, and no phosphorylation is involved in this step.
o: Pyruvic acid gets converted to acetyl Co.A by phosphorylation
It enters mitochondrial matrix and undergoes oxidative decarboxylation
It undergoes reduction to form ethanl and CO₂
It remains in cytoplasm and undergoes oxidative decarboxylation

t: Identify the step where second oxidative decarboxylation occur in respiration
s: The first oxidative decarboxylation is pyruvic acid → acetyl CoA in the link reaction. The second occurs in the Krebs cycle when α-ketoglutaric acid is oxidatively decarboxylated to succinyl CoA, releasing CO₂ and forming NADH. The oxalosuccinic acid step is treated as a simple decarboxylation following an oxidation.
o: Oxalo succinic acid → α- ketoglutaric acid
α - ketoglutaric acid → Succinyl Co. A

t: In a single turn of TCA cycle, in how many points, NAD⁺is reduced to NADH+H⁺?
s: In one turn of the TCA cycle NAD⁺ is reduced to NADH + H⁺ at three steps: isocitrate → oxalosuccinate (α-ketoglutarate), α-ketoglutarate → succinyl CoA, and malate → oxaloacetate. One FADH₂ is formed at succinate → fumarate, and one GTP by substrate level phosphorylation.

t: Which of the following is false regarding respiration
s: Prokaryotes lack mitochondria; their respiratory enzymes are in the cytoplasm and the ETS lies on the plasma membrane. So statement A is false. Aerobic respiration gives a net yield of 38 ATP per glucose theoretically, the RQ of tripalmitin is about 0.7, and pyruvate dehydrogenase converts pyruvate into acetyl CoA.
o: In prokaryotic organisms, the respiratory enzymes are present in the mitochondrial matrix.
In aerobic respiration, respiratory output is 38 ATP.
The R.Q. value is 0.7, when tripalmitin is used as respiratory substrate.
Pyruvic dehydrogenase is used in converting pyruvic acid into acetyl Co-A.

t: In oxidative phosphorylation, (A) is the ultimate acceptor of electrons and it gets reduced to water. Identify (A)
s: Oxygen is the ultimate (terminal) acceptor of electrons in the ETS. Cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV) passes electrons to O₂, which combines with protons to form water: ½O₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂O. OAA is a Krebs cycle compound, while cytochrome a₃ and FMN are intermediate carriers.

t:
Assertion (A) : During TCA cycle, GTP is synthesized by substrate level phosphorylation.
Reason (R ) : GTP is synthesized during the conversion of succinic acid into fumaric acid
s: The assertion is true: GTP (or ATP) is formed by substrate level phosphorylation in the Krebs cycle. The reason is false because GTP is formed during conversion of succinyl CoA to succinic acid. Conversion of succinic acid to fumaric acid reduces FAD to FADH₂, not GTP.
o: (A) is false but ( R) is true

t: In respiration
s: In glycolysis fructose-1,6-bisphosphate splits into two triose phosphates, and dihydroxyacetone phosphate is converted to PGAL, so two PGAL (glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate) are formed per glucose. The Krebs cycle has no PGAL, as it deals with acetyl CoA, citrate and other organic acids.
o: 2 PGAL are fomed in glycolysis and none in Krebs cycle
6 PGAL in glycolysis, 3 PGAL in Krebs cycle
8 PGAL in glycolysis, 3 PGAL in Krebs cycle
PGAL formation does not occur in respiration

t:
Identify the incorrect statement from the following options :
[[img:a67039b0905f]]
s: The incorrect statement is D. In anaerobic respiration pyruvic acid is converted to CO₂ and ethanol by pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase, or to lactic acid by lactate dehydrogenase. Pyruvic acid dehydrogenase works in aerobic respiration. Statements A, B and C correctly describe fermentation.
o: The incomplete oxidation of glucose is achieved under anaerobic conditions
In muscles during exercise the pyruvate gets converted into lactic acid
Yeasts poison themselves to death when the concentration of alcohol reaches about 13 per cent
The enzymes pyruvic acid dehydrogenase and alcohol decarboxylase catalyse these reactions

t: Which product of glycolysis is consumed in alcoholic fermentation?
s: In alcoholic fermentation pyruvic acid is decarboxylated to acetaldehyde, which is reduced to ethanol using NADH + H⁺ produced in glycolysis by alcohol dehydrogenase. This regenerates NAD⁺. ATP is not consumed in fermentation, and CO₂ is a product, not a substance consumed.

t: In electron transport system (ETS) which of the following cytochromes reacts with oxygen
s: In the ETS cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV) contains cytochromes a and a₃ along with two copper centres. Cytochrome a₃ transfers electrons directly to molecular oxygen, reducing it to water. Cytochrome b is in complex III, and b₃ and b₆ are not in the mitochondrial chain.

t: In Krebs cycle
s: In the Krebs cycle, succinyl CoA is converted to succinic acid with substrate level phosphorylation of GDP to GTP, which can form ATP. Pyruvic acid is converted to acetyl CoA before the cycle, glucose is broken in glycolysis, and CO₂ and H₂O are not formed from pyruvate directly.
o: Pyruvic acid is converted into O₂ and H₂O
Pyruvic acid is converted into ATP

t:
Identify the incorrect statement from the following options :
[[img:41191a752bab]]
s: The citric acid cycle contains 6C (citric acid), 5C (α-ketoglutaric acid) and 4C compounds (succinic acid, malic acid, oxaloacetic acid). It contains no 3C compound. Pyruvate (3C) is converted to acetyl CoA (2C) in the link reaction before entering the cycle, so the statement about a 3C compound is incorrect.

t: Enzymes of Krebs cycle occur in mitochondrial matrix except one which is attached to inner mitochondrial membrane
s: All Krebs cycle enzymes are located in the mitochondrial matrix except succinate dehydrogenase, which is bound to the inner mitochondrial membrane. It is also part of complex II of the ETS and transfers electrons from succinate through FADH₂ to ubiquinone.

t: Aerobic respiration is
s: Aerobic respiration is the complete oxidation of organic substances such as glucose in the presence of oxygen, releasing CO₂, water and a large amount of energy. Incomplete oxidation without oxygen is anaerobic respiration or fermentation, so option B is correct.
o: The process in which complete oxidation of organic substances occur in the absence of oxygen
The process in which complete oxidation of organic substances occurs in the presence of oxygen
The process in which incomplete oxidation of organic substances occurs in the absence of oxygen
The process in which incomplete oxidation of organic substances occurs in the presence of oxygen

t: Krebs cycle starts with the formation of six carbon compounds by reaction between
s: The Krebs cycle starts with condensation of the 2C acetyl group of acetyl CoA with 4C oxaloacetic acid and water, catalysed by citrate synthase, to form the 6C citric acid and release CoA. Malic, succinic and fumaric acids are intermediates, and pyruvic acid does not enter directly.

t: Oxidation of pyruvate to CO₂ and H₂O occurs through
s: Pyruvate is completely oxidised in two stages: the link reaction converts pyruvate to acetyl CoA, NADH and CO₂, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle oxidises acetyl CoA to CO₂. The reduced coenzymes are oxidised in the ETS to form H₂O. So both link reaction and TCA cycle are involved.

t: Which of the following enzyme/s is/are absent in mitochondria
s: Invertase (sucrose hydrolysis) and hexokinase (glycolysis) act in the cytoplasm, so they are absent in mitochondria. Citrate synthase is a Krebs cycle enzyme present in the mitochondrial matrix, so only options 1 and 3 are absent.

t: Which of the followng is not a part of any complex in ETS?
s: Ubiquinone and cytochrome c are mobile electron carriers in the ETS. Ubiquinone moves within the inner membrane from complexes I and II to complex III, and cytochrome c moves from complex III to complex IV. Cytochrome a₃ is part of complex IV, so both 1 and 2 are not parts of any complex.

t: Which of the following process is used in the conversion of pyruvate to acetyl CoA?
s: Pyruvate is converted to acetyl CoA by the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex through oxidative decarboxylation: pyruvate + CoA + NAD⁺ → acetyl CoA + CO₂ + NADH + H⁺. CO₂ is removed (decarboxylation) and NAD⁺ is reduced (oxidation). It is not phosphorylation or dehydration.

t: For each ATP produced, how many H passes through F₀ from the intermembrane space to the matrix down the electrochemical proton gradient?
s: According to NCERT, for each ATP produced 4 H⁺ ions pass through F₀ of ATP synthase from the intermembrane space to the matrix down the electrochemical proton gradient. The energy of this proton flow is used by F₁ to form ATP from ADP and Pi.

t: The F₁ and F₀ of oxysome is a/an ____ and ____
s: In ATP synthase (oxysome), F₁ is the headpiece, a peripheral membrane protein complex that contains the site for ATP synthesis. F₀ is an integral membrane protein complex forming the channel through which protons cross the inner membrane. They are protein complexes, not lipid or steroidal complexes.
o: Integral membrane steroidal complex, peripheral membrane steroidal complex
Integral membrane lipid complex, peripheral membrane lipid complex
Integral membrane protein complex, peripheral membrane protein complex
Peripheral membrane protein complex, integral membrane protein complex

t: R.Q is less than one if the respiratory substrate is
s: RQ = volume of CO₂ evolved / volume of O₂ consumed. Fats and proteins are poor in oxygen, so they require more O₂ for oxidation and their RQ is less than one, e.g. tripalmitin RQ about 0.7. Carbohydrates such as glucose and sucrose give RQ = 1, and organic acids give RQ more than 1.

t: How many decarboxylations are present in a single Krebs cycle
s: In a single Krebs cycle turn two decarboxylations occur, both releasing CO₂: oxalosuccinic acid → α-ketoglutaric acid and α-ketoglutaric acid → succinyl CoA. The third CO₂ of each pyruvate is released in the link reaction, which is not part of the cycle.

t: Identify the first member of Krebs cycle
s: The Krebs cycle begins when acetyl CoA condenses with oxaloacetic acid, which acts as the acceptor molecule and is regenerated at the end. Oxaloacetic acid is considered the first member of the cycle, while citric acid is the first product. Pyruvic acid and acetyl CoA are not members of the cycle itself.

t: How many oxidations, decarboxylations and substrate level phosphorylations are there in a Krebs cycle
s: One turn of the Krebs cycle has 4 oxidations (dehydrogenations: isocitrate, α-ketoglutarate, succinate, malate → 3 NADH + 1 FADH₂), 2 decarboxylations (oxalosuccinate → α-ketoglutarate and α-ketoglutarate → succinyl CoA, releasing 2 CO₂) and 1 substrate level phosphorylation (succinyl CoA → succinate, forming GTP/ATP). Hence 4, 2, 1.

t: Which of the following enzyme is required for both Krebs cycle and ETS
s: Succinate dehydrogenase oxidises succinate to fumarate in the Krebs cycle and is also complex II of the ETS, passing electrons from FADH₂ to ubiquinone. Citrate synthase and pyruvic dehydrogenase work only in the cycle/link reaction, while NADH dehydrogenase (complex I) belongs only to the ETS.

t:
Consider the following statements and select the correct option:
Statement I : Movement of protons from intermembrane space towards the matrix occur through Fₒ requires energy
Statement II : Proton gradient occur across the inner membrane of mitochonrdia during electron transport
s: Statement I is false: protons move from the intermembrane space back into the matrix through the F₀ channel passively, down their concentration (electrochemical) gradient; this flow releases energy used by F₁ to make ATP, it does not consume energy. Statement II is true: electron transport pumps protons out of the matrix, creating a gradient across the inner membrane.

t: Total number of substrate level phosphorylation occur when two molecules of acetyl co-enzyme A enter in to Krebs cycle:
s: Each acetyl CoA entering the Krebs cycle gives one substrate level phosphorylation, when succinyl CoA is converted to succinic acid with formation of GTP (→ATP). Two acetyl CoA molecules mean two turns of the cycle, so there are two substrate level phosphorylations in total.

t:
Identify the active transport process occur during cellular respiration :
A) Pumping of protons from perimitochondrial space towards the matrix
B) Pumping of protons from matrix towards the perimitochondrial space
C) Flow of protons from perimitochondrial space to the matrix
s: Active transport needs energy and moves ions against their gradient. During electron transport, complexes I, III and IV use the energy of electron flow to pump protons from the matrix into the perimitochondrial (intermembrane) space, against the gradient. Protons flowing back into the matrix through F₀ move down the gradient (passive), so only B is active transport.

t: Which of the following is false about Krebs cycle:-
s: Statement D is false: CO₂ is released twice in each Krebs cycle turn, during oxalosuccinate → α-ketoglutarate and α-ketoglutarate → succinyl CoA decarboxylations. The others are true: α-ketoglutaric acid is the only 5C intermediate, GTP is formed by substrate level phosphorylation, and citric acid is the first stable product (hence the name citric acid cycle).
o: Alpha Ketoglutaric acid is the only 5C compound during Krebs cycle
Substrate phosphorylation occurs during Krebs cycle.
Citric acid is the first stable product in Krebs cycle
There is no release of CO₂ during Krebs cycle.

t:
Which stages of aerobic respiration takes place in mitochondria
i) Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvic acid
ii) Glycolysis
iii) Krebs cycle
iv) Oxidative phosphorylation
s: Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate (link reaction), the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation all occur in mitochondria: the first two in the matrix and the last on the inner mitochondrial membrane. Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm, so options containing ii are wrong. Hence i, iii and iv.

t: How many reduced co-enzymes are formed with in the mitochondria during complete oxidation of one glucose molecule
s: Per glucose, mitochondria produce 2 NADH in the link reaction (2 pyruvate → 2 acetyl CoA) and, from two Krebs cycle turns, 6 NADH + 2 FADH₂. Total reduced coenzymes = 2 + 6 + 2 = 10. The 2 NADH of glycolysis are formed in the cytoplasm, not inside mitochondria.

t:
Assertion : A single turn of Krebs cycle yields 24 ATP molecules
Reason : In one Krebs cycle, 3NADH+H⁺,1FADH₂ and 1 GTP molecules are formed
s: The Assertion is false: one turn of the Krebs cycle yields 3 NADH (9 ATP) + 1 FADH₂ (2 ATP) + 1 GTP (1 ATP) = 12 ATP; 24 ATP come from two turns (one glucose). The Reason is true, correctly stating the products of one turn: 3 NADH + H⁺, 1 FADH₂ and 1 GTP.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but reason is not correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

t: The process that is common for the following three steps
s: All three steps release CO₂, so decarboxylation is the common process. Pyruvate → acetyl CoA and α-ketoglutarate → succinyl CoA are oxidative decarboxylations (dehydrogenation + decarboxylation), but oxalosuccinate → α-ketoglutarate is a simple decarboxylation without dehydrogenation. Dehydration does not occur in any of them. Hence decarboxylation (option 2) is common.
o:
Alphaketoglutaric acid → Succinyl Co.A
(1) Dehydrogenation
(2) Decarboxylation
(3) Dehydration

t: Pyruvate, after it enters mitochondrial matrix undergoes oxidative decarboxylation by the action of which enzyme?
s: In the mitochondrial matrix, pyruvate undergoes oxidative decarboxylation catalysed by the pyruvic dehydrogenase complex (with Mg²⁺, NAD⁺ and CoA), forming acetyl CoA, NADH and CO₂. Citrate synthase forms citrate in the Krebs cycle, invertase hydrolyses sucrose and hexokinase phosphorylates glucose in glycolysis.

t:
Assertion : 2 molecules of ATP are produced from one molecule of pyruvic acid during the conversion of it into Acetyl Co. A.
Reason : The FADH₂ produced during this conversion can release 3 ATP molecules through oxidative phosphorylation.
s: Both are false. Conversion of one pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA produces one NADH + H⁺ (not FADH₂), which on oxidative phosphorylation gives 3 ATP, not 2 ATP. No FADH₂ is formed in the link reaction, and FADH₂ gives only 2 ATP anyway, so the Reason is also incorrect.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but reason is not correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false

t:
Assertion : Complex I and complex V of ETS are NADH dehydrogenase and ATP synthase respectively.
Reason : Cytochrome c acts as a mobile carrier for transfer of electrons between complex II and complex III.
s: The Assertion is true: complex I is NADH dehydrogenase and complex V is ATP synthase (F₀–F₁). The Reason is false: cytochrome c is a small mobile carrier that transfers electrons between complex III (cytochrome bc₁) and complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase); ubiquinone carries electrons from complexes I and II to III.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but reason is not correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false

t: Which of the following statement is false?
s: Statement D is false: fats are poor in oxygen relative to carbon and hydrogen, so more O₂ is consumed than CO₂ released and the RQ is less than one (about 0.7, e.g. tripalmitin 102 CO₂/145 O₂). The other statements are true: pyruvate is 3C, acetyl CoA forms in the matrix, and NADH₂ forms in both glycolysis and Krebs cycle.
o: Acetyl Co A is formed in matrix due to oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate
NADH₂ is formed during glycolysis and Krebs cycle
When fats are used in respiration, the RQ is greater than one

t: In which of the following reaction of glycolysis, a molecule of water is removed from the substrate
s: Conversion of 2-phosphoglycerate to phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) is catalysed by enolase and involves removal of one water molecule (dehydration). Fructose-6-phosphate → fructose 1,6-bisphosphate is phosphorylation, PGAL → 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate is oxidation (dehydrogenation) with phosphorylation, and PEP → pyruvate is substrate level phosphorylation.

t: How many substrate level phosphorylations are occur in glycolysis when 1 molecule of pyruvic acid is formed
s: Each pyruvate arises from one triose (PGAL), which yields two ATP by substrate level phosphorylation: 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate → 3-phosphoglycerate, and PEP → pyruvic acid. So formation of one pyruvic acid involves two substrate level phosphorylations (four per glucose).

t: Which is not true for glycolysis?
s: Glycolysis ends with pyruvic acid (with net 2 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose), not CO₂ and H₂O; CO₂ and water are end products of complete aerobic oxidation via Krebs cycle and ETS. Glycolysis does spend 2 ATP (hexokinase and phosphofructokinase steps) and produces 4 ATP by substrate level phosphorylation.
o: End products are CO₂ and H₂O

t: The enzyme Hexokinase is present in:-
s: Hexokinase catalyses the first step of glycolysis, phosphorylation of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate. Since glycolysis takes place entirely in the cytoplasm, hexokinase is a cytoplasmic enzyme. It is not present in mitochondria (site of link reaction, Krebs cycle and ETS) or in the vacuole.

t: The reaction involved in the conversion of 2-phosphoglyceric acid into 2-phosphoenol pyruvic acid, during glycolysis
s: 2-phosphoglyceric acid is converted into phosphoenol pyruvic acid by enolase with removal of a water molecule, i.e. dehydration. No CO₂ is released (not decarboxylation) and no hydrogen is removed (not dehydrogenation or oxidative decarboxylation). This dehydration creates the high energy phosphate bond of PEP.

t:
Count the number of true statements :
i) Fat is the favoured substrate for respiration.
ii) Complex carbohydrates are usually first converted into monosaccharides before they are used for respiration.
iii) Sucrose is converted into glucose and fructose by the enzyme, invertase, and these two monosaccharides can readily enter the glycolytic path way.
iv) Fats & proteins never used purely as substrates.
v) Fats would need to be broken down into glycerol and fatty acids first; if fatty acids were to be respired they would first be degraded to acetyl Co. A and enter the pathway; glycerol would enter the pathway after being converted to PGAL.
s: Statement i is false: carbohydrates, not fats, are the favoured respiratory substrate. Statements ii, iii, iv and v are true as per NCERT: complex carbohydrates are first converted to monosaccharides, invertase splits sucrose into glucose and fructose, fats and proteins are never used purely as substrates, and fats enter via acetyl CoA (fatty acids) and PGAL (glycerol). So four are true.

t:
Consider the following statements and select the correct option :
Statement I: With respect to cellular respiration in mitochondria, chemiosmosis occur through complex I, III and IV.
Statement II : Diffusion of protons occur from intermembrane space to matrix through F₀ part of oxysome.
s: Statement I is false: complexes I, III and IV pump protons (creating the gradient), whereas chemiosmotic ATP synthesis occurs through complex V (F₀–F₁ ATP synthase). Statement II is true: protons diffuse passively from the intermembrane space back into the matrix through the F₀ channel of the oxysome, driving ATP synthesis by F₁.
o: Statement I and II are false
Statement I and II are true

t:
Consider the following statements :
A) FMN present in complex I only
B) Fe-S protein present in more than one enzyme complexes
C) Cytochrome a and cytochrome a₃ are present in complex IV only
D) Final electron acceptor present in complex V
Of the above statements ;
s: FMN is the prosthetic group of complex I only; Fe-S proteins occur in complexes I, II and III; cytochromes a and a₃ with copper are present in complex IV only. Statement D is false: the final electron acceptor, oxygen, is reduced at complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase), not complex V, which is ATP synthase. Hence all except D are true.
o: A, B and C are false

t: FAD⁺acts as a hydrogen acceptor during the oxidation of
s: In the Krebs cycle, succinate dehydrogenase oxidises succinic acid to fumaric acid and the hydrogen is accepted by FAD, forming FADH₂. Oxidation of pyruvic acid, malic acid and α-ketoglutaric acid uses NAD⁺ as hydrogen acceptor, forming NADH + H⁺.

t: In which of the following enzyme complex proton pumping does not occur
s: Complexes I, III and IV act as proton pumps, moving H⁺ from the matrix to the intermembrane space. Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase) transfers electrons from FADH₂ to ubiquinone without pumping protons, and complex V (ATP synthase) lets protons flow back into the matrix rather than pumping them. Hence complex II and V.

t:
The three boxes in this diagram represent the three major biosynthesis pathways in aerobic respiration. Arrows represent net reactants or products.
[[img:d0f55658875f]]
Arrows numbered 11 and 12 respectively
s: The three boxes are glycolysis (A), link reaction plus Krebs cycle (B) and electron transport with oxidative phosphorylation (C). Pathway C receives NADH, FADH₂, O₂, ADP and Pi, and its net products are water (O₂ is the final electron acceptor, reduced to H₂O) and ATP. So arrows 11 and 12 are H₂O and ATP.

t:
How many of the following statements are true:
[[img:850e3349abf7]]
s: All four statements are true. In fermentation, NADH₂ is oxidised back to NAD⁺ while reducing pyruvate; in glycolysis, NAD⁺ is reduced to NADH₂ during PGAL oxidation; conversion of pyruvate to ethanol or lactic acid involves no substrate level phosphorylation; and both glycolysis and fermentation use internal organic acceptors, not external ones like O₂. Hence four.

t: How many oxygen molecules are consumed in glycolysis when two molecules of pyruvic acids are formed in cytoplasm:
s: Glycolysis is an anaerobic process occurring in the cytoplasm; oxygen is not required at any step. PGAL is oxidised by NAD⁺, not by O₂. Hence zero oxygen molecules are consumed when two pyruvic acid molecules are formed from glucose. O₂ is consumed only as the final electron acceptor in the ETS.

t: Which of the following is/are formed after oxidative decarboxylation in Krebs cycle ?
s: Within the Krebs cycle, the only oxidative decarboxylation is α-ketoglutaric acid → succinyl CoA (by α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase), releasing CO₂ and NADH. Acetyl CoA is formed by oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate in the link reaction, which precedes the Krebs cycle, and pyruvic acid is formed in glycolysis.

t: The three complexes (I, II and III) of mitochondrial ETS
s: Complexes I (NADH dehydrogenase), II (succinate dehydrogenase) and III (cytochrome bc₁) all contain iron-sulphur (Fe-S) centres. Complex II does not pump protons, only complex I oxidises NADH, and only complex II oxidises FADH₂, so options A, C and D do not apply to all three. Fe-S as cofactor is common.

t: Phosphoenol pyruvate is formed from 2-phosphoglyceric acid by
s: Enolase converts 2-phosphoglyceric acid into phosphoenol pyruvate by removing one molecule of water (dehydration). No CO₂ is added or removed in this step, and water is lost rather than added. The resulting high energy phosphate bond in PEP is later used to make ATP.

t: One ATP is formed when
s: In the Krebs cycle, succinyl CoA is converted to succinic acid by succinyl CoA synthetase; energy of the thioester bond forms GTP (which gives ATP) by substrate level phosphorylation. Succinate → fumarate produces FADH₂, α-ketoglutarate → succinyl CoA produces NADH and CO₂, and fumarate → malate is hydration.

t: Which of the following is incorrect about enzyme 'Hexokinase'
s: Statement C is incorrect: hexokinase is precisely the enzyme that phosphorylates glucose, converting it to glucose-6-phosphate using ATP in the first step of glycolysis. As glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm of both prokaryotes and eukaryotes, hexokinase is present there, so A, B and D are correct.
o: It is present in cytoplasm of both prokaryotes and eukaryotes
It helps in the conversion of Glucose to Glucose-6-phosphate
It cannot help in the phosphorylation of glucose
It catalyze the first step of glycolysis

t: There can be a net gain of 38ATP molecules during aerobic respiration of one molecule of glucose. Out of this 38ATP molecules how many are formed through substrate level phosphorylation ?
s: Substrate level phosphorylation gives net 2 ATP in glycolysis (4 formed minus 2 used) and 2 ATP (as GTP) from two Krebs cycle turns, i.e. 4 ATP. The remaining 34 ATP of the 38 are produced by oxidative phosphorylation in the ETS from 10 NADH₂ and 2 FADH₂.

t: Oxidative decarboxylation of respiratory intermediates results in the formation of
s: Oxidative decarboxylation (removal of hydrogen and CO₂ together) occurs in two places: pyruvate → acetyl CoA, NADH₂ and CO₂ in the link reaction, and α-ketoglutarate → succinyl CoA, NADH₂ and CO₂ in the Krebs cycle. Pyruvic acid is a product of glycolysis, not of oxidative decarboxylation. Hence both 1 and 2.

t: The respiratory balance sheet prepared for one molecule of glucose is based on certain assumptions. Which of the following is not one of them ?

t: How many water molecules are generated in ETS when reduced coenzymes ( NADH₂ and FADH₂ ) from one glucose molecule are completely oxidised
s: Each pair of electrons passing to O₂ forms one water molecule (½O₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂O). One glucose yields 10 NADH₂ (2 glycolysis, 2 link, 6 Krebs) and 2 FADH₂, i.e. 12 reduced coenzymes. Their complete oxidation in the ETS generates 12 water molecules.

t: How many reduced coenzymes are formed from two molecule of pyruvic acid after oxidative decarboxylation and krebs cycle reactions?
s: Each pyruvate gives 1 NADH in oxidative decarboxylation and, in one Krebs cycle turn, 3 NADH + 1 FADH₂, i.e. 5 reduced coenzymes. Two pyruvate molecules therefore give 2 × 5 = 10 reduced coenzymes (8 NADH₂ and 2 FADH₂).

t: When two molecule of glucose participate in Krebs cycle in the form of acetyl Co.A, how many oxidations occur in it:
s: Each acetyl CoA entering the Krebs cycle undergoes 4 oxidations (isocitrate, α-ketoglutarate, succinate and malate dehydrogenation). Two glucose molecules give 4 pyruvate → 4 acetyl CoA, so 4 turns × 4 oxidations = 16 oxidations.

t: How many redox equivalents are removed from PGAL and how many co-enzymes are accepted by them during the oxidation of one molecule of glucose in glycolysis respectively
s: One glucose gives two PGAL molecules. Each PGAL is oxidised to 1,3-bisphosphoglyceric acid by losing two redox equivalents (hydrogen atoms), accepted by one NAD⁺. So two PGAL lose 4 redox equivalents, accepted by 2 NAD⁺ coenzymes, forming 2 NADH + H⁺.

t: Identify the total production of ATP during anaerobic respiration and are formed through the process of
s: Anaerobic respiration (fermentation) involves only glycolysis followed by reduction of pyruvate. Glycolysis produces a total of 4 ATP by substrate level phosphorylation (2 at 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate and 2 at PEP), giving net 2 ATP after using 2. No oxidative phosphorylation occurs, because NADH is reoxidised by pyruvate or acetaldehyde, not by the ETS.

t: In lactic acid fermentation, electrons and protons from substrate are transferred by
s: In lactic acid fermentation, NAD⁺ accepts hydrogen (electrons and protons) during glycolysis when PGAL is oxidised, forming NADH + H⁺. Lactate dehydrogenase then transfers these from NADH to pyruvic acid, reducing it to lactic acid and regenerating NAD⁺. FAD is not involved, and ethanol is the product of alcoholic, not lactic, fermentation.

t: When two molecule of glucose participate in Krebs cycle in the form of acetyl Co-A, how many decarboxylations occur in it
s: Each Krebs cycle turn has 2 decarboxylations (oxalosuccinate → α-ketoglutarate and α-ketoglutarate → succinyl CoA). Two glucose molecules give 4 pyruvate → 4 acetyl CoA, i.e. 4 turns of the cycle, so 4 × 2 = 8 decarboxylations occur in the Krebs cycle.

t: Which of the following enzyme complexes are involved in electron transport system when NADH₂ is the electron donor?
s: NADH₂ is oxidised by complex I (NADH dehydrogenase); electrons pass via ubiquinone to complex III, then via cytochrome c to complex IV, which reduces O₂ to water. The proton gradient so formed drives ATP synthesis through complex V. Complex II is used only when FADH₂ (from succinate) is the donor, so complexes I, III, IV and V are involved.
o: Complex I, III, IV and V
Complex II, III, IV and V

s: Only statement A is true: the acetyl group condenses with oxaloacetic acid and water to form citric acid, releasing CoA (citrate synthase). t:
Krebs cycle occur when :
A) Only carbohydrates are oxidising in cell
B) Only fat are oxidising in cell
C) Only proteins are oxidising in cell
D) Only in the presence of oxygen
E) In the presence or absence of oxygen
F) Carbohydrates, fat and proteins are oxidising in cell
s: The Krebs cycle is a common pathway: carbohydrates, fats (via acetyl CoA and glycerol) and proteins (via deaminated amino acids) are all oxidised through it. It operates only in the presence of oxygen, because NAD⁺ and FAD reduced in the cycle can be reoxidised only through the ETS with O₂ as final acceptor. Hence D and F.

Statement II is false: protons are pumped from the matrix into the intermembrane space by the ETS complexes, and flow back passively from the intermembrane space to the matrix through the F₀ channel, not pumped through F₀−F₁. Both are false.
o: Statement I and II are false
Statement I and II are true
